gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the CD receivers' power on one basis: the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT's '22 W RMS' (as Sonic Electronix lists it) is Pioneer's continuous rating. Under the CTA-2006 standard it is 14 W RMS x 4. Sony's MEX-N5300BT is 20 W RMS x 4 under CTA-2006, so the cheapest card ChatGPT showed has the weakest built-in amp, even though both units list '50–55 W' on the box.
standout_why: Of the results ChatGPT got, I compared pioneerofficial.com (rank 4), sonicelectronix.com DEH-S4220BT (rank 14), abt.com (rank 6) and the JVC USA page (rank 5). pioneerofficial.com lists '14 W RMS x 4-ch (CTA-2006)' next to '22 W continuous' but gives no test conditions and no comparison with other brands. Sonic Electronix calls the 22 W figure 'RMS' with no standard named. Abt gives only 'MOSFET 50W x 4'. The JVC page lists no power figure at all. ChatGPT's answer quoted no power or preamp figures. Part of the finding is already on a rival page; the side-by-side comparison on one basis is not. I could not load Crutchfield's cited guide (HTTP 403), so I could not check whether it has CTA-2006 figures.
decides: This settles the pick only for a shopper running the factory speakers off the head unit. On CTA-2006 power the Sony MEX-N5300BT (20 W x 4) beats the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT (14 W x 4), and the Sony has a third (subwoofer) preamp pair while the Pioneer has two. Someone adding an external amp would weigh preamp voltage instead: the Pioneer is 4 V at Abt. For the Sony, Sonic Electronix lists 4 V and MobileSpecs lists 2 V, so that figure is unsettled. The '22 W RMS' figures for the Kenwood KDC-BT282U and JVC KD-T920BTS stay unsourced, so I can't yet say which brand has the strongest amp.

findings.label: Power ratings as listed (max / continuous / CTA-2006)
findings.value: 50 W x 4 max (4 Ω); 22 W x 4 continuous; 14 W RMS x 4 CTA-2006 (4 Ω)
findings.note: The page lists all three figures separately and gives no THD or frequency conditions for the 22 W one. This domain is not Pioneer's US store (usa.pioneer) and shows a $45.99 sale price, which may mean a lookalike store. Use its spec text only, never its price. I could not open usa.pioneer (HTTP 429) to confirm.

findings.label: Retailer's 'RMS' figure (actually the continuous rating)
findings.value: Peak 50 W x 4; 'RMS' 22 W x 4 (no standard or conditions named)
findings.source_title: Pioneer DEH-S4220BT CD Receiver with Bluetooth | Sonic Electronix
findings.note: The 22 W matches Pioneer's continuous figure, not the 14 W CTA-2006 figure. This is the footnote: the same unit shows up as 22 W 'RMS' or 14 W RMS depending on the page. Sonic's price is $149.99 (list $180.00). 2 sets of 4 V preamp outputs, no dedicated subwoofer output, 13-band EQ, FLAC up to 192 kHz/24-bit.

findings.label: Price, preamp outputs, EQ, formats
findings.value: $149.99; 2 pairs RCA preouts at 4 V; 13-band EQ (31-band with the Pioneer Smart Sync app); CD/CD-R/RW, MP3, WMA, AAC, WAV, FLAC; amp listed only as 'MOSFET 50W x 4'
findings.note: This is the retailer behind ChatGPT's $149.99 card. Abt lists '5-Phone CONNECTION (A2DP)' and 'Dual Phone Connection (HFP)'.

findings.label: Power, preamp outputs, price
findings.value: Peak 55 W x 4; RMS 20 W x 4; 3 sets (6-channel) preamp outputs incl. subwoofer, listed as 4 V; $158.00 (list $159.99); 10-band EQ; FLAC; Dual Bluetooth (two phones)
findings.note: No RMS test conditions on this page. The page title also says 'MEX-N5200BT' in one place, and its reviews are for the MEX-N5000BT.

findings.label: CTA-2006 power and preamp voltage
findings.value: 20 W RMS x 4 (CTA-2006, 20 Hz–20 kHz); peak 55 W; preamp 2 V
findings.source_title: Sony MEX-N5300BT specifications and reviews | MobileSpecs
findings.note: A third-party spec database with no source cited. It agrees with Sonic on 20 W RMS but disagrees on preamp voltage (2 V vs Sonic's 4 V). Sony's own spec pages returned HTTP 403.

findings.label: What the maker page states
findings.value: 13-band EQ; two phones connected full time over Bluetooth (up to 5 devices for Streaming DJ); HFP 1.7; no power or preamp figures on the page

findings.label: Normalised built-in amp power (CTA-2006 RMS per channel, 4 channels)
findings.value: Sony MEX-N5300BT 20 W vs Pioneer DEH-S4220BT 14 W; Sony is about 43% higher (20 / 14 = 1.43), although the box headlines are close (55 W vs 50 W) and retailers list the Pioneer as '22 W RMS'
findings.note: Arithmetic combines the Pioneer CTA-2006 figure (this page) with the Sony CTA-2006 figure (https://mobilespecs.net/car-receivers/Sony/Sony_MEX-N5300BT.html, read 2026-11-10). Both are second-hand. Confirm against the maker manuals before publishing.
